title: "Lab 15B: AI Conclusion and Caption Review"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

## Goal

Audit polished generated prose at the claim level and replace it with a concise
conclusion whose numbers, scope, and limitations agree with the evidence.

## Scenario

Download and run:

- [week15-ai-conclusion-review.R](../code/r/week15-ai-conclusion-review.R)

The generated paragraph uses correct vocabulary and one correct numerical
comparison. It also introduces causation, universal accuracy, unsupported
generalization, an undeclared replacement model, and a claim that limitations
are negligible.

## Part A: Segment The Paragraph

Underline each independently checkable claim. Separate linked claims joined by
“so,” “therefore,” or “because”; a correct premise does not guarantee a correct
conclusion.

## Part B: Verify Every Number

Recalculate validation RMSE, baseline RMSE, sensitivity RMSE, and largest
absolute error. Record the exact source and displayed rounding for each value.

## Part C: Complete The Claim Audit

For every generated claim, record:

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict | Repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weather causes high ozone |  |  |  |
| Model RMSE is below baseline RMSE |  |  |  |
| Every September day is accurate |  |  |  |
| The model generalizes to all seasons |  |  |  |
| Sensitivity refit should replace the model |  |  |  |
| Limitations are negligible |  |  |  |

## Part D: Check Logical Connectors

For each “so” or “because,” decide whether the second clause follows from the
first. Replace overstrong connectors with wording that matches the evidence.

## Part E: Repair The Caption

Write a caption for the observed-versus-predicted figure that names the 29-row
September subset, explains the identity line and labeled error, reports one
checked performance comparison, and states one limitation.

## Part F: Write The Final Conclusion

Write 5-7 sentences covering:

- the question and validation setting;
- model-versus-baseline evidence;
- one important failure or diagnostic;
- sensitivity result without replacing the frozen model;
- association rather than causation;
- limits on generalization.

Every numerical value must trace to a named artifact.

## Part G: Draft The AI-Use Entry

Record the task given to the LLM, the paragraph received, the checks performed,
the five rejected or repaired claims, and the group member who reviewed the
final wording.

## Deliverable

Submit the segmented paragraph, numerical verification table, completed claim
audit, connector review, repaired caption, final conclusion, and AI-use entry.

## Exit Question

Complete this sentence:

> A polished conclusion becomes evidence-based only when ...
